identity.trade: The ferry and the garrison: Blackwater holds the crossing on the outer road, and every cart pays the toll to the watch.

greeting: Quiet watch. Keep it quiet.
Blackwater is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: Recruits come, officers go. The ledger says we are even.
The beacon on the hill was lit for a moment last night and put out. Nobody ordered it.
A toll-keeper swears the black water takes a coin every spring.

opinions.tobin_hazelden: Tobin is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.morning: Dawn drill. You are in the way.

dialogue.aside: You came. I am delighted. I have rehearsed this expression.

greeting: Sit anywhere that is not wet. The wet ones are the regulars.
State your business and stand where I can see you.
rumour: Soldiers pay on pay day and owe the rest of the month. I keep two ledgers.
Travellers say the stones are dimmer on the east road. I water the ale, not the news.
A sentry saw a figure on the wall, tall and still. By the time he called out, nothing.
The Blackwater Ford Post drew a stranger last month. He asked questions and bought nothing.

opinions.hedda_coldwell: Hedda has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Hedda.

time.evening: Evening watch. Stand easy, but not too easy.

dialogue.aside: Hmph. You again. Fine. Sit. I did not say I was glad.

greeting: Mind the anvil. It has opinions.
You will hear Blackwater before you see it. Ask at the Blackwater Ford Post.
rumour: Spear heads, mail repair, shield bosses. The army eats iron.
The forge hums when the stones dim. Not loud. Enough to notice.
A cart of provisions came in with a weapon crate hidden under the grain. No papers.

opinions.hanne_buckley: Hanne has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Hanne.
opinions.seren_jessop: Seren lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.night: Night watch. If you hear something, say nothing. Tell me.

dialogue.aside: Hello. A pause. I am glad you came. That is all.

greeting: Everything has a price. Some of it is even written down.
The Blackwater Ford Post is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: Whetstones and bandages go first. I try not to think about what that means.
Folk buy more than they need, then bring half back. Fear shops strangely.
Wolves test the line at dusk. Men test it at dawn. We hold either way.
If trade slows, Blackwater feels it first. If it speeds up, Blackwater feels it last.

opinions.gunnar_wainwright: Gunnar undercuts me. I forgive Gunnar. Mostly.
opinions.hedda_coldwell: Hedda keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.rain: Rain on the wall. The sentries grumble. The mud grumbles louder.

dialogue.aside: Friend, you know I will not change my mind. Ask anyway. I enjoy refusing you.

greeting: Bread is at dawn. After dawn it is a rumour.
Strangers in Blackwater get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: A sack of flour came in short, twice. The miller swears by his scales.
Old soldiers say the wall is built on something older. They stop talking when a recruit walks past.
The watch rode out three nights ago and came back with fewer men.

opinions.calder_thorpe: Calder keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.
opinions.seren_jessop: Seren undercuts me. I forgive Seren. Mostly.

time.morning: Dawn drill. You are in the way.

dialogue.aside: Mind the order of things, friend. There. Now we can talk.

greeting: Sit. Tongue out. No, the other way.
First time in Blackwater? The Blackwater Ford Post is the place to start.
rumour: Fever in two households. Nothing the stones can mend.
The armoury is short on arrowheads. The smith is short on iron. The iron is short on road.

opinions.gunnar_wainwright: Gunnar lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.evening: Evening watch. Stand easy, but not too easy.

dialogue.aside: Eh? Oh, it is you. I heard that. I always hear friends.

greeting: Quiet town. Good. Do not make it noisy.
Folk come to Blackwater for ferry and garrison. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: My night watch wants a second lantern each. I want a second night watch.
Recruits are keener since the stones dimmed. Keen is not the same as ready.
Bandits ask the watch the toll before they hit the road. A joke, sort of.

opinions.lorne_redfern: Lorne knows the trade. I will say that for Lorne.
opinions.tobin_hazelden: Tobin works hard and talks harder.

rumour: Captain says it is nothing. Captain also says that about rain.
Messengers get thinner every month. Messages get shorter. That is the real pattern.
The Blackwater Ford Post has seen odder days than this. Nobody remembers when.

dialogue.aside: Excuse the dust. Work does not stop for friends, though it does pause.

greeting: Evening. Stones are lit, gate is shut, I am cold.
Blackwater is ferry and garrison. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Heard something past the hedge last night. Whatever it was, it was not honest.
The ditch and stakes held last winter. Barely. Nobody wants a harder test.

dialogue.aside: Welcome, welcome. Your name is right there. On the tip of my tongue.

greeting: Sit by me. My knees insist.
Discipline is the one wall that needs no mortar.
rumour: The old stones had names. Nobody writes them down. Nobody asks me.
Messengers ride in at night and out before dawn. They wear no colours.
Folk say Blackwater was founded by someone who wanted to be left alone. We have not forgotten.

opinions.tobin_hazelden: I would trust Tobin with a purse. A small one.

time.evening: Evening watch. Stand easy, but not too easy.

dialogue.aside: I dreamed of you last night. You were a heron. It suited you.

greeting: Come closer. My ears are old and your voice is young.
Welcome to Blackwater. Mind the Blackwater Ford Post. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Winters were colder, summers longer, and the wolves stayed home. Or so I choose to remember.
Ask anyone in Blackwater about the Blackwater Ford Post. You will get four stories and one fact.

greeting: Fare first, then the story. In that order.
rumour: The river carried a lantern past last night, floating upright. Nobody sent it.
Blackwater lives by ferry and garrison. When that fails, so do we.

rumour: Rope goes missing in lengths, not coils. Somebody is cutting, not stealing.
